videos.script: A container's filesystem dies with the container. So does a pod's, with the pod. And pods are replaced all the time. {{dies}} Anything worth keeping has to live somewhere the pod does not own. Kubernetes splits that problem in three. {{three}} A PersistentVolumeClaim is the application asking: I need one gibibyte, writable by one node. A PersistentVolume is a real piece of storage that answers it. And a StorageClass is the recipe that makes a new volume whenever a claim asks. {{objects}} You will lose data on purpose, then keep it across a deleted pod, and then find out what deleting the claim does to the data. The default answer surprises people. {{plan}}
